results.title: Deep learning for precipitation nowcasting: A survey from ...
results.content: The outputs predicted by recursive strategy tend to blur with increasing forecast times (Whang et al., 2022) when DL models are trained with global-level loss functions, e.g., MAE or MSE. When predictive models are applied to precipitation datasets with highly mixed dynamics, the DL models often constrain diverse space-time deformations (Yao et al., 2023). NowCasting-nets (Ehsani et al., 2022) compared the performance of UNet-based and RNN-based models for 90 min forecasting using satellite and radar inputs. The Fourier-based precipitation nowcasting, such as fast Fourier transform (FFT), can help extract relevant features and improve the performance of forecasting models (Wu et al., 2023, 2024). Full global model emulators such as FourCastNet (Pathak et al., 2022), Pangu-Weather (Bi et al., 2022), GraphCast (Lam et al., 2022), and Gencast (Price et al., 2023) are capable of predicting three-dimensional atmospheric fields for medium range time scale (typically 5 – 10 days) although precipitation forecast has not been their strong point.
